title: Priority inversion: a futex storm with more softirq and less migration

problem.summary: Low-priority threads hold a lock that higher-priority work needs, and the scheduler keeps them off the CPU. It looks like lock contention because it IS lock contention - the difference is in how the threads move between CPUs and how much soft-interrupt work surrounds them.
symptoms: a service is slow and its CPU is not saturated
the slowdown is worse than the offered load explains
some requests are far slower than others

discriminators.signal: futex share, which puts it in the lock family
discriminators.not_this_problem: a deadlock sits at 4.3%; the stress and network families at 0%
discriminators.evidence: MEASURED on 41 labelled runs across 8 families with blueprints/lib/fingerprint_table.py (22-09-2026). priority_inversion 41.0% (n=5) against deadlock 4.3% (n=5).

discriminators.signal: softirq share, which separates it from plain lock contention
discriminators.not_this_problem: lock contention sits at 5.9% (n=5), less than half
discriminators.evidence: MEASURED on 41 labelled runs across 8 families with blueprints/lib/fingerprint_table.py (22-09-2026). softirq 13.4% vs 5.9%, migrate 2.0% vs 5.0%, both n=5. WEAK: futex alone does not separate them (41.0 vs 47.0), so these two secondary numbers carry the decision and a verdict here should carry lower confidence than one for its siblings.

discriminators.signal: threads migrate LESS than under plain contention
discriminators.this_problem: migrate 2.0% (n=5) - they are held off CPU, not bouncing
discriminators.evidence: MEASURED on 41 labelled runs across 8 families with blueprints/lib/fingerprint_table.py (22-09-2026). migrate 2.0% vs 5.0% (n=5 each).

unverified_do_not_claim.claim: the inversion can be seen directly in scheduler priority fields
unverified_do_not_claim.status: NOT MEASURED - and it is the check that would settle it
unverified_do_not_claim.measurement: sched_switch carries prev_prio and next_prio in its payload, but our count index keeps counts only, so priority was never read. The recipe uses nice-based inversion, not SCHED_FIFO, so the priorities are there to be read.
unverified_do_not_claim.consequence: the two secondary shares carry this blueprint today. Reading prev_prio/next_prio per container would likely give a decisive discriminator and is the single most valuable thing to add.

reproduction.teardown: the recipe restores state; verify against /sys/fs/cgroup
harness_only: the fault is injected as a sidecar container, which is a property of our harness. In production the same mechanism occurs inside an existing service - so the SHAPE transfers, the newcomer shortcut does not

collection_order.why_these: MEASURED BASIS. Every discriminator in this blueprint is a share of these event groups within one container. Nothing else in the trace is required, and no other modality is used - this blueprint was built and validated on kernel traces alone.

processing.expect: a CTF directory with metadata and channel streams

processing.step: Find containers that are active during the window and absent before it
processing.expect: one container with substantial traffic during the window and none before. If none appears, this blueprint does not apply - say so and stop

processing.step: Measure what share of its own events that container spends on each kind of work
processing.expect: the share profile below, within the measured range

processing.step: Apply the rules and emit the verdict
processing.expect: a verdict naming the container and the mechanism, or an explicit abstain
one page showing the shares, the cut, and what was ruled out

outputs.contains: culprit container pid_ns, its event shares, and the shares of every other container for comparison
per-container event shares for the window
each family's measured share on the deciding axis, with this run's value marked

verdict_when: a container is new to the window
its share profile matches the measured range below
no sibling container shows the same profile

rule_out.when: migration is around 5% and softirq around 6%, measured against 2.0% and 13.4% here
futex falls to a few percent and the container goes nearly silent

decision.root_cause_is: the container whose threads hold a lock while being scheduled away

provenance.authored_by: measured from StrataTrace v2 kernel traces
provenance.notes: Built 22-09-2026 from blueprints/lib/fingerprint_table.py over 41 labelled runs of 8 families. Candidate signals were first put through discover_signature.py (a specificity sweep across families, which rejected unlinkat, ftruncate, block_split, lseek and dup as window artefacts) and who_makes_it.py (which rejected the nagle_delayed_ack host-wide signal as 94% our own load generator). KERNEL TRACES ONLY - no metrics, logs or spans were consulted.

apply_when: a service is slow without CPU saturation
a container shows a high futex share
do_not_apply_when: the container is nearly idle - see deadlock-lock-order
applicability.cheap_precheck: a container with a futex share above 40% and softirq above 10%

stopping_conditions.conclude: the share profile matches and no sibling container matches it too
stopping_conditions.stop_and_switch: a discriminating share falls outside its measured range
stopping_conditions.stop_insufficient: no container is new to the window and none stands out

applicable_symptoms: a service is slow and its CPU is not saturated
the slowdown is worse than the offered load explains
some requests are far slower than others

historical_effectiveness.note: shares measured on 5 runs of this family

evidence_sufficiency.if_below_floor: report the shares and say which blueprint they sit between
evidence_sufficiency.report_when_stuck: the container's shares and every sibling's, side by side
